newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan leads in UN race but French oppose him.
newsitem.headline: Annan leads in UN race but French oppose him.

text.p: Kofi Annan of Ghana, the U.N. official in charge of peacekeeping, on Wednesday increased his lead in the race for the U.N secretary-general but France apparently still opposed him, diplomats said.

The envoys said that in the initial unofficial ballot on Wednesday, Annan had received 12 votes in favour, and three against, one of them presumably from France, which has veto power. He had received 10 votes at the end of polling in the 15-member Security Council on Tuesday.

Annan's closest rival, the diplomats said, was Amara Essy, the foreign minister of Ivory Coast, who came in second again with 7 votes in favour, 4 against, two of them from the United States and Britain.
In order to win, a candidate must have a minimum of nine votes and no veto. France, the United States, Britain, Russia and China have veto power on the council.

If the polling continues in the same pattern, Annan is left as the only candidate among the four before the council now. The next step, diplomats said, might be high-level discussions to persuade France to change its mind or possibly throw the race open to Asian nominess if the contest on African candidates is deadlocked.

Votes were not immediately available on Hamid Algabid of Niger, secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference, and Ahmedou Ould-Abdallah of Mauritania, a former U.N. special envoy for Burundi, but envoys said the votes for both men fell below those for Annan and Essy. U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, whose term expires on December 31, has temporarily stepped aside in the race following a November 19 U.S. veto of his candidature.
